title: M9: Machine code and assembly lessons (machine, assembly, then C)
description: Intent: As the student, I want the first programming lessons to start with machine code, then move up to assembly, then to C, so that I understand what the computer actually does before using higher-level languages. Includes: a teaching instruction set with an emulator, an assembler and disassembler, Monaco language support (syntax highlighting, hover docs, error markers) for both machine code and assembly, a stepping view (registers, memory, program counter, flags) in the IDE, runnable examples for lessons, and a path from assembly lessons to C lessons. Excludes: full real-world ISAs (x86-64, ARM64) for now; showing compiler-generated assembly for C is a possible later lesson. Open design decision recorded in a comment: which instruction set. DoD: the student can type machine code (bytes) and assembly in the IDE, run and single-step it, see registers and memory change, and the same program works in both forms; every behavior has a passing Gherkin spec.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Direction (2026-10-06): ISA is RISC-V RV32IM (fixed 32-bit, no compressed) so machine code, assembly and compiled C share the same instructions; custom toy CPU dropped. Compilation Explorer = linked source, assembly, machine code and bit fields, with an in-browser TypeScript emulator. An outside review (opus) agreed with the idea but advised a short pedagogy pilot and a corpus/toolchain spike; the maintainer chose to build the whole vertical slice now (library, /explain endpoint, web UI) and take the pilot in parallel. Rust and C++ in the explorer are deferred. Detailed plan and curriculum design are in progress.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Slice A merged (PRs #13, #14): @sierrendipity/explorer — RV32IM decoder with bit fields, assembler, machine-code parser, and an emulator with step back, breakpoints and the Linux ecall ABI. Verified against independent references: two review rounds (encodings and emulator semantics vs a BigInt reference), GNU as and objdump differential on 255 words, and the official riscv-tests (48 of 48 rv32ui/rv32um, fence_i and ma_data skipped by design). Slices B (/explain + runtime) and C (web UI) in progress.

right_now_summary: The team is building a RISC-V learning slice with an emulator, compiler endpoint, and linked web explorer.
